_comment: Qwen Code agents for any project, nothing to edit: run `node <agent-network-mcp>/dist/index.js ui --runners <agent-network-mcp>/examples/runner/runners.qwen.example.json` inside your project (a git repository with at least one commit). The project is the repository you start it in.

defaults.worktree: every agent works in its own git worktree next to the project, <project>-<agent> on branch swarm-<agent>, created at start when missing (from the project's HEAD); the network is <project>/.agent-network, kept out of git through .git/info/exclude. Give an agent a "cwd" to put it elsewhere. Several projects on one page: copy this file per project and add "project": "/abs/path/to/it".
{agentNetworkMcp} is this repository's folder (the loader fills it in), so the file works where it lies; a copy elsewhere works too.

--max-session-turns 70: short sessions on purpose. Every turn reads the whole context again, so one 200-turn session costs several times more than three of 70. A session that reaches the limit after doing something is a planned end, not a failure: the runner starts a fresh one at once and tells it to go on from git status and its subtasks.
qwen does not expand ${AGENT_ID} in --mcp-config but passes its environment to MCP servers: the runner sets AGENT_ID and NETWORK_DIR.
Prompt first, right after qwen: --allowed-tools takes several values and would swallow it.
instructionsFile (per agent, relative to this file): the agent's own instructions, appended to the standard prompt and read again before every session; can also be set on the page.
stream-json output lets the runner count tokens and cost per session (task statistics) and still show a readable log.

Lean context: a short system prompt ({systemPrompt} <- systemPromptFile) and only the tools the agent needs; every turn re-reads them, so this cuts tokens per turn several times. The skill tool is not excluded, so the agents can load skills from .qwen/skills/ in their folder (java-dev-flow); add "skill" to --exclude-tools when they need none: every turn re-reads the skill list.

git: only the commands the protocol needs (status, diff, log, show, add, commit, merge, rev-parse); reset, branch -D, push are declined in headless mode (checked on Qwen Code 0.24.7). Add a command only when an agent really needs it.

Model: the command has {model}; "model" is the default (an agent can have its own), "models" is the choice in the runner card on the page (applies from the next session). Ids as the model server lists them, e.g. curl http://<lm-studio>:1234/v1/models.
prices: USD per 1M tokens for the models whose CLI reports no cost (Qwen); 0 = a free local model, or put a provider's prices to see what the work would cost there. Read again when the file changes.
autostart: false = start that agent with the button on the page.

supervisor: the agent that looks after the others (page tab «Надзор»), here on Qwen Code with a model from LM Studio. A detector without a model checks the swarm every 10 s; on an incident it starts one supervisor session with the tools of qwen-supervisor-mcp.json (qwen passes AGENT_NETWORK_UI_URL and the rest of its environment to the MCP server). Shell and file writes are excluded: it acts through the page and frees hung tests and database locks; decisions only you can take come to the page as «нужно ваше решение». Its cost is counted with "prices" (0 for a local model); budgetUsd is checked against that. Switch it on/off, pick the model and its tools on the page.

supervisor.tools: your own commands for it, argv without a shell; {agentCwd} adds an agentId parameter (the agent's folder), {projectDir}/{networkDir} are filled in, own params are checked (type, enum, pattern). "action": true for a command that changes something: each run goes into its journal. disabledTools switches any tool off (also on the page).

schedules: tasks the page creates by itself on a cron (local time; @daily, @weekdays = Mon-Fri 9:00, ...), no model involved. A run is skipped while the previous task of the same schedule is still open. {date} and {time} in title/description are filled in. Off here ("enabled": false): switch it on on the Tasks tab or here.

Subagents: the agent tool is not excluded, so an agent can start the subagents of .qwen/agents/ in its folder for bounded side jobs. Only the agent itself talks to the swarm (the system prompt says so); give subagents tools without mcp__agent-network. Add "agent" to --exclude-tools to switch subagents off.

The helper subagent of Qwen is a file: copy examples/runner/qwen-agents/helper.md to ~/.qwen/agents/ once (every project and worktree sees it), or to .qwen/agents/ of the project and commit it. --max-subagent-depth 1: a subagent starts no subagents of its own.

The model server is http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1 (LM Studio on this machine); another host: change --openai-base-url in both commands (agents and supervisor). The MCP servers are given inline (--mcp-config takes JSON); "timeout" (ms) lets the build tool run up to 30 min (Qwen stops MCP calls after 10 min by default).

maxTaskCostUsd: the cost limit of a task created on the page or by a schedule (all its sessions together, priced with "prices" since Qwen reports no cost); reached, the task is BLOCKED until you raise it (+$ on the page) or cancel it. Remove it for no limit.

run_shell_command(openspec): the author of a change-writing task (task create --propose, or «+ написать новый change…» on the page) creates and validates the change with the openspec CLI (openspec new change, instructions, validate).

tools.name: surefire_failures
tools.description: Test report files with a failure or an error in an agent's folder (target/surefire-reports, failsafe-reports): read them with Read

tools.name: agent_git_log
tools.description: The latest 15 commits of an agent's worktree branch

tools.name: testcontainers
tools.description: Docker containers started by Testcontainers: id, image, how long they run, name

schedules.title: Flaky tests {date}
schedules.description: Run the full test suite twice (./mvnw -q -B verify -Dsurefire.timeout=900). Fix tests that fail only sometimes: shared state, ordering, time, ports, container reuse. Production code stays as it is unless a test proves a real bug; then ask the operator. In result: which tests were flaky, why, what you changed.
